title: Unveiling Maternal-fetal BRAin-body Interactions in Pregnant WOmen Affected by Depression
official: Unveiling Maternal-fetal BRAin-body Interactions in Pregnant WOmen Affected by Depression
summary:
The goal of this study is to learn how depression during pregnancy is linked to changes in the brain and body of the mother and to the development of the baby, in pregnant women with major depressive disorder (MDD) and pregnant women without depression.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How common is major depressive disorder during pregnancy in a European multi-site cohort?
* Do pregnant women with MDD show differences in hippocampal volume compared with pregnant women without depression?
* Do maternal blood, placenta, cord blood, brain imaging and heart activity measures, and the brain and development of the babies, differ between the two groups?

Pregnant women will be screened within the 20th week of pregnancy and assigned to the MDD group or to the control group based on a structured clinical interview. They will not receive any study drug: women with depression will receive the usual care recommended by clinical guidelines.

Participants will:

* Have clinical, psychiatric and psychological assessments (interviews and questionnaires) at screening, at 22, 26 and 32 weeks of pregnancy, at birth, and at 1 and 6 months after birth
* Have a brain MRI with simultaneous EEG-ECG or photoplethysmography (PPG) at about 22 weeks of pregnancy
* Have a fetal MRI by 22 weeks and fetal ultrasound scans at 22, 26 and 32 weeks
* Give blood samples at 22, 26 and 32 weeks of pregnancy, and a cord blood sample at birth (placenta samples in a subgroup at the Milan center only)

Their newborns will have a neurological and visual examination, a brain MRI and an EEG-ECG or PPG recording after birth, and a developmental assessment (Bayley Scales) at 6 months.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Pregnant women with major depressive disorder (Group 1):

* Signed informed consent and ability to understand and provide it
* Age between 18 and 45 years
* IQ \> 70 (4 subtests of WAIS-IV: Vocabulary, Similarities, Block Design, Matrix Reasoning)
* Diagnosis of major depressive disorder according to the SCID-5-CV at screening (within 20 gestational weeks)

Pregnant women without depression (Group 2):

* Signed informed consent and ability to understand and provide it
* Age between 18 and 45 years
* IQ \> 70 (4 subtests of WAIS-IV: Vocabulary, Similarities, Block Design, Matrix Reasoning)
* No current or past psychiatric disorders (SCID-5-CV)
* No family history of psychiatric disorders (SCID-5-CV and FIGS)

Placental tissue sampling (Milan only, Groups 1 and 2):

* Elective cesarean delivery
* Absence of labor

Newborns:

* Informed consent signed by both parents
* Full-term birth (gestational age at birth of 37 weeks or more)

Exclusion Criteria:

Pregnant women (Groups 1 and 2):

* History of head trauma with loss of consciousness
* Neurological or degenerative disorders
* Comorbid psychiatric disorders
* Twin pregnancy
* Pregnancy resulting from assisted reproductive technology with egg donation
* History of perinatal alcohol or drug abuse
* Infectious or autoimmune diseases
* Use of systemic corticosteroids
* Congenital, genetic or neurological disorders affecting the mother or the fetus
* Body mass index (BMI) \> 30
* Severe prior obstetric conditions
* Absolute or relative contraindications to MRI

Newborns:

* Congenital, genetic or neurological disorder of the newborn
